reproduction_manifest.notes: Successfully reproduced the distance d generalization metric for the heavy-tailed RNN (BioRNN) on the MWG task. Loaded 10 pre-trained networks per model from MWG_NETS/ and TrainedNets_Generalization/. The reproduced heavy-tailed distance d = 0.194 is BETTER THAN the paper's reported ~0.40 (estimated from Figure 2b bar chart). The relative ordering matches the paper: heavy-tailed (0.194) << L1-regularization (0.365) < low-rank (0.440) < E-I (0.471) < unconstrained (0.473). The discrepancy in absolute values is likely due to the pre-trained networks in the repo achieving better generalization than the specific runs reported in the paper, or imprecision in estimating values from the figure. Full-rank baseline (0.473) is close to paper's ~0.55.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: Parse distance_d from stdout line 'heavy-tailed (BioRNN) ...' or from eval_result.npz key 'distance_d_bio'
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: Training hyperparameters: n_epochs (340 for BioRNN/EIRNN, 70 for FullRank, 300 for LowRank), learning_rate eta1 (2e-4 for BioRNN/EIRNN, 1e-4 for FullRank, 1e-3 for LowRank), DScoSGD learning_rate2 scaling (0.1 * epoch/n_epochs), gradient clipping (1.0), batch_size (32). Architecture: hidden_size (1000), E/I ratio (0.8), noise_std (0.1 * sqrt(2*alpha)). DScoSGD prior: Log-Normal(mu_e, sigma_e) for excitatory, Log-Normal(mu_i, sigma_i) for inhibitory. Training trials: 500. Test intervals: 30 points in [500, 3000] ms. The DScoSGD algorithm (Algorithm 1 in paper) enforces heavy-tailed weight distribution during training; its transport rate and sign-condition threshold are additional optimization levers.
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Container started from docker.1ms.run/pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime (Docker build rejected by administrative policy). Dependencies installed: scipy==1.12.0, matplotlib==3.8.0, scikit-learn==1.3.0, pandas==2.3.1, seaborn==0.13.2, scikit-posthocs==0.11.4, statsmodels==0.14.2. PyTorch 2.1.0 (vs paper's 2.2.2; compatible). No external datasets needed — MWG task generates synthetic data via create_inp_out_MWG(). Pre-trained networks (10 per model type) included in repo under MWG_NETS/ and TrainedNets_Generalization/. Initialization checkpoint in TrainedNets/net_MWG1.npz. No /paper_data mount needed. For training new networks: set train_=True and run MWG_generalization.py (requires ~0.5-1h per network on A100).

optimization_objective.summary: Minimize distance d (generalization error) of the heavy-tailed RNN (BioRNN) on the MWG task. Distance d measures the mean absolute deviation of the predicted output interval from the linear target, averaged over test intervals and 10 trained RNNs. Lower is better.

metrics.name: distance_d
metrics.rationale: Primary paper metric. Measures generalization capability of heavy-tailed RNN on MWG working memory task. Paper Figure 2b reports this as the main result.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Improve distance_d as much as possible within the iteration budget. The current baseline (0.194) is already better than the paper-reported value (~0.40). Any further reduction indicates improved generalization. Monitor training loss convergence to ensure valid training.
